candidates.source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (hirdetmények / eljárások)
candidates.why_relevant: Mandatory national e-procurement platform: essentially all Hungarian public procurement procedures must be run in EKR. Tender documentation (műszaki leírás) for ATM operation, POS terminal supply, card personalisation and cash-logistics contracts is published here free of charge, typically containing fleet counts, transaction volumes, SLA levels and unit prices — hard quantitative data disclosed for legal reasons.
candidates.source_subtype: national e-procurement platform / tender documentation repository
candidates.access_status: public browsing of notices; full documentation download at https://ekr.gov.hu/portal/kozbeszerzes/eljarasok/ (registration may be required for some functions)
candidates.legal_status: official state system, public data by law (Kbt.)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic scripted browsing of the hirdetmények/eljárások lists filtered by CPV and keyword; download attached documentation PDFs; respect rate limits, session/JS-heavy portal may need headless browser
queries_used: EKR Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer ekr.gov.hu közbeszerzés

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Közbeszerzési Értesítő (official procurement bulletin)

Below-EU-threshold and national notices — including ATM operation, cash transport, ticket-vending machine and payment-IT contracts — are published here with subject, estimated/awarded value and winning bidder. Confirmed to hold banking/cash-relevant notices (e.g. banknote-processing machine purchase, cash transport awards).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Stable per-notice permalinks (/ertesito/{year}/0/targy/portal_xxx/megtekint/portal_ID_year/) allow deterministic crawl; scrape by date and subject-category with CPV/keyword filter
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from search results

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Adatbázis – hirdetménykereső (Public Procurement Database search)
candidates.why_relevant: Searchable back-end of the Hungarian procurement registry: notices and contract documents by contracting authority, CPV code (incl. obsolete codes) and free text. The most efficient single entry point for systematic CPV-driven retrieval of ATM/POS/card/cash-handling contracts across years.
candidates.legal_status: public data under Kbt. transparency rules

candidates.source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (EU OJ supplement), Hungary notices
candidates.why_relevant: All above-EU-threshold Hungarian contracts (large ATM outsourcing, national card-personalisation, cash-in-transit frameworks, core payment IT) must be published on TED, in structured eForms with CPV codes, estimated and awarded values, and winning economic operators. Gives cross-border comparability and the cleanest machine-readable form of the same data as Közbeszerzési Értesítő.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the documented TED Search API (expert queries: country=HUN + CPV + date range) rather than HTML scraping; supplement with daily/monthly XML bulk packages
queries_used: TED tender Hungary payment terminals card services contract notice
TED Europa data API notices Hungary XML bulk download

candidates.source_name: TED Open Data Service / data.ted.europa.eu
candidates.why_relevant: Bulk, structured open-data distribution of TED notices — enables longitudinal analysis of Hungarian ATM/POS/cash contract values, buyer concentration and vendor market shares over many years without page-by-page scraping.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled download of monthly XML packages (https://ted.europa.eu/packages/monthly/{yyyy-n}), filter country=HU and target CPVs into a local warehouse

negative_findings.description: Targeted Hungarian-language search for POS-terminal public procurement notices ('POS terminál közbeszerzés eredmény hirdetmény keretszerződés bankkártya') returned only commercial bank/acquirer marketing pages (OTP, Erste, MBH, SimplePay) and generic Public Procurement Authority pages — no specific POS-terminal tender.
negative_findings.result_summary: Generic web search is a poor channel for POS-terminal tenders; the term 'POS terminál' is dominated by acquiring-service marketing noise.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: POS terminal procurement in Hungary is largely private-sector (banks/acquirers) and therefore outside Kbt.; the public-procurement channel will yield POS mainly via state-owned buyers, transport ticketing and municipal cash-desk systems. Retrieval must be done inside EKR/Értesítő/TED with CPV filters, not via open web search.

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian card-personalisation (kártyaszemélyesítés / kártyagyártás) procurement notice or dedicated buyer channel was located in this pass; searches surfaced only TED/CPV background material, not an actual HU notice.
negative_findings.result_summary: Card-personalisation tenders not confirmed in this run.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card personalisation for Hungary is mostly commissioned by commercial banks and card processors (private, not Kbt.-bound), so public tenders may exist only for state-linked issuers (e.g. Magyar Posta, state health/ID cards, transport cards). The cell's card-personalisation coverage is therefore weak and needs a dedicated CPV-driven pass.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice was fetched and verified for liveness; all entries are search-derived with permalink patterns observed in results. EKR and TED portals are JavaScript-heavy and may return 403/challenge to naive fetchers.
negative_findings.result_summary: Liveness and crawlability are hypotheses, not verdicts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream deterministic verification must distinguish bot-defence (403/timeout, likely live) from genuine relocation (404). Do not mark EKR/TED as dead on a single failed fetch.

negative_findings.description: Searches for cash-in-transit incumbents surfaced only one concrete award (Magyar Posta cash transport/processing won by MPT Security Magyar Posta Takarék Biztonsági és Logisztikai Zrt., stated value 80,000,000 HUF in a 2020-era Értesítő record); no systematic list of Hungarian CIT procurement was assembled.
negative_findings.result_summary: Cash-logistics vendor landscape only partially mapped from procurement notices.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cash-logistics incumbency (MPT Security, and international CIT operators) is a core intelligence target; a CPV-based sweep on security/cash-transport codes is still required.

coverage_gaps.description: State-owned and state-influenced banks (e.g. MBH Bank group entities, Magyar Fejlesztési Bank, Takarék entities, Magyar Posta's financial arms, Diákhitel Központ) were not individually checked for buyer-profile procurement pages or as 'ajánlatkérő' in the procurement registry.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run an ajánlatkérő-name sweep in the Közbeszerzési Adatbázis and EKR for each state-linked financial institution; capture their notices on ATM fleets, card issuing and payment IT.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV-code-driven sweep was executed; the pass relied on keyword search. CPV families for cash dispensers, payment/banking terminals, smart cards, card production, cash-in-transit security services and banking software were not enumerated against HU notices.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the CPV list from ted.europa.eu/en/simap/cpv, then query both the TED Search API (country=HUN) and the Hungarian hirdetménykereső per code, for at least the last 10 years.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal and utility contracting entities (parking companies, water/energy utilities, hospitals, universities) that buy card-accepting terminals, parking payment machines and cash-desk systems were not sampled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Sample the largest municipalities (Budapest districts, county seats) and parking operators in the procurement database for 'parkolóautomata', 'bankkártyás fizetés', 'kártyaelfogadó terminál'.

coverage_gaps.description: Remedies and dispute channels (Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság decisions, Állami Számvevőszék audits of procurement, court/appeal records) were identified only via the registries hub, not individually located as sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and add the Döntőbizottság decision database and ÁSZ audit-report search as separate sources — appeals often expose bid prices and technical specifications that were otherwise redacted.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian-language coverage was strong for ATM/cash terms, but no local-language terms were exercised for card personalisation and card issuing ('kártyaszemélyesítés', 'kártyagyártás', 'chipkártya', 'kártyakibocsátás') or for payment IT ('kártyaelfogadói rendszer', 'tranzakciós switch', 'ATM monitoring rendszer').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the glossary with these terms and re-run both open-web and in-portal searches; record which yielded hits.

coverage_gaps.description: Contract-modification notices ('szerződésmódosításról szóló tájékoztató') and performance/completion notices were not treated as a distinct collection stream, although they are where actual delivered quantities and extended fleet counts appear.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated collector for modification and performance notices tied to previously captured ATM/POS/cash contracts.

brief: Hungary's procurement channel for payments intelligence is unusually well-structured: EKR (ekr.gov.hu) carries the full procedure documentation for essentially every domestic tender, the Közbeszerzési Hatóság publishes the Közbeszerzési Értesítő and a CPV-searchable database of notices and contracts, and above-threshold contracts duplicate onto TED with a free, authentication-free Search API and monthly XML bulk packages — making a deterministic CPV-driven pipeline entirely feasible. The richest quantitative disclosures for our topics come from state-linked buyers: Magyar Posta (cash transport and cash processing, incumbent MPT Security), the MNB (banknote-processing systems with multi-year maintenance), and transport operators BKK and MÁV, whose ticket-vending-machine tenders quantify unattended card-acceptance fleets and even the cash-vs-card mix (card share above 70% of BKK automat purchases; dozens of card-only devices). Demand is currently being driven by statute: the 2025. évi XVIII. törvény and 19/2025 (VI.26.) MNB rendelet mandate ATM installation in every settlement of 1,000+ residents and force joint installation/operation contracts between payment service providers, so an ATM procurement wave should be visible in these channels. The main weaknesses of this cell are POS terminals and card personalisation, which in Hungary are mostly bought by private banks and processors outside the Public Procurement Act, and the absence so far of a systematic CPV sweep — both should be closed before treating procurement as a complete indicator of fleet size or vendor share.
